Title: Amphora of Panathenaic Shape
Description: This vase is shaped like the vases of oil given as prizes at the Panathenaic Festival, a music and athletic contest in Athens.

Title: Late Corinthian Round Aryballos
Description: Two hoplites (Greek armored footsoldiers) wearing Corinthian helmets battle with spears.

Title: Early Corinthian Round Aryballos
Description: The vase bears a decorative four-leaf design known as a quatrefoil.  The floral design, of Near Eastern origin, invokes the smell of the aromatic oil or perfume in the container.

Title: Red-Figure Lekythos
Description: Winged Nike, the goddess of victory, extends a libation bowl with her right hand and holds a kithara (harp) with her left.

Title: Red-Figure Askos
Description: Two male deer gallop toward the spout.  Vessels like these may have been used to hold liquids like wine, oil, honey or vinegar in small quantities.

Title: Red-Figure Squat Lekythos
Description: The sphinx, a mythical animal, stands with one paw over a wreathed altar.  She is a guardian figure, usually associated with graves.

Title: Polychrome Lebes Gamikos
Description: Polychrome vases were designed only for display, usually in funerary contexts. One male and two female figures are barely discernable on the body of this vase.

Title: Polychrome Oinochoe
Description: The faded scene on the body features Eros, the god of love, leading the four-horsed chariot of Nike, the goddess of victory.

Title: Pelike
Description: Winged Eros, the god of love, chases a fawn. Pots like this, known as Gnathian ware, often bear ornate decoration.

Title: Red-Figure Fish Plate
Description: Octopus, flatfish, squid, and shellfish, native to this part of the Mediterranean, decorate this plate.  The depression in the center may have been meant to hold sauce or juices from cooked fish.

Title: Black-Figure Kyathos
Description: Dionysus, god of wine, is seated between two satyrs and framed by two monstrous eyes. The shape of the vessel is specifically Etruscan and imitates metal prototypes.

Title: Middle Corinthian Stemless Kylix
Description: Real and mythical animals, including lions, boars, sphinxes, and panthers, parade through the three decorative zones.  These animals, popular decoration on Corinthian vases, originate in Near Eastern art.

Title: Red-Figure Kantharos
Description: Two-handled cups of this shape were strongly associated with Dionysus, the god of wine, and were especially popular in the Greek region of Boeotia.

Title: Black-Figure Oinochoe
Description: The Greek hero Herakles fights the Nemean Lion. The skin of this lion will become the hero’s most prominent attribute.

Title: Red-Figure Hydria/Kalpis
Description: The meaning of the scene is unclear today, but similar elements in other Apulian vases suggest that its significance would have been understood by an Apulian audience.

Title: Black-Figure Neck-Amphora
Description: Athena, goddess of wisdom, drives a four-horse chariot.

Title: Red-Figure Kylix – Type B
Description: Two athletes use strigils (scrapers) to scrape olive oil from their bodies.

Title: Black-Figure Kylix – Type A
Description: A gorgoneion, the fierce face of the mythical Gorgon -- a female monster also known as Medusa -- turns away evil and reminds the drinker of the dangers of excess.

Title: Red-Figure Kylix – Type B
Description: The youth on left holds a strigil (scraper) while the man on the right leans on the forked staff of a trainer.

Title: Red-Figure Column-Krater
Description: Ariadne, the daughter of the mythical king Minos of Crete, steps into a four-horse chariot.  Dionysus stands behind the horses.

Title: Red-Figure Bell Krater
Description: The naked youth on left plays a lyre and a girl plays an aulos (reed pipe), while the youth to the right seems to direct movement with a torch, leading a lively procession.

Title: Geometric Amphora
Description: Pots of this type were used in graves. Neck panels feature meander patterns, while vertical leaves on the body look forward to naturalistic figurative motifs that became prevalent after 700 BCE.
